reason: Idle runners burned 16% of a core each because every map.changed made every handler re-read the store. The fix was a concern filter on the event plus waits on events instead of sleep loops. This is a class of work (bus event handlers, waits, idle CPU), so it is born as one umbrella rule, not a session-shaped note.

Episode fixed a missing Rule 4 (coalesce bursts) in the runner's own-ticket path, added kinds-only announcements for state changes, and documented two remaining collection reads. The existing skill covers the filter-first rule but none of these, so a future handler would reintroduce the per-event spawn.
The current trigger only names map.changed handlers; the episode showed the same burn in the runner and the web server, which a future session would search for by those words.

The polling sweep produced a repeatable procedure: find the timer and loop sites, keep stream readers and real deadlines, convert the rest, and pin the kept set in a guard test. The skill covers waits but not how to sweep or classify them.
Handler flag set before checking whether the event changed anything caused a needless write per start; the fix and its rule are reusable across every event handler that marks dirty.

A fixed-sleep quiet window in an idle-read test is timing-dependent; it passed alone and failed under combined load. The fix (open the window on an emitted signal) and the combined-run check are reusable for every such test.

Episode ticket #32 (no polling) surfaced concrete event-path techniques the skill lacks: dirty-flag-on-change, uvicorn main_loop override, checking an upstream's own live stream before keeping a timer, and the Windows lock wait. This skill was loaded and is the one that governs them.

The dock agent-list change added a redraw to two existing event paths. The rule for a gated, read-free draw on an existing path, with a mutation check, is missing here. The episode also skipped the 60 s CPU reading this skill requires, so the bullet points at it.

Lesson from the dispatch wait polling fix: a write with no tables/kinds made the launch wait wake on the runner's own insert, which breaks Rule 3 (never react to your own writes). The existing bullet covers naming concerns but not the bare-write failure mode.

Lesson from the dispatch wait fix: an empty work_ids list is a known answer (no ticket concerned), distinct from an absent field (unknown). The skill's field rule does not say which, and the fix had to correct its wording on this point.

Lesson from the dispatch wait fix: coalescing a waiter's named-ticket reads between passes, with a full read on the first pass and after any change that does not say which tickets. The skill covers coalescing for checks but not for waits.

Lesson from the dispatch wait fix: measuring idle CPU alone misses wake-ups, and the before/after comparison ran cleanly by launching both old and new trees side by side from a copy, which the shared-checkout rule favours over stashing.

Episode replaced the view's 2 s and 2.5 s client timers with server-held reads because the host pushes nothing to views. The held-read shape (wait on change, deadline per call, re-ask on answer, backoff only on failure) is a reusable event-path rule that this skill governs and was loaded for.

The episode added a uvicorn exit-wait subclass inside the mcp module, while this bullet says one shared chassis copy; the conflict was not surfaced. The rule needs its out-of-scope case so the next session names the duplicate rather than adding a silent third.
Supersedes the held-read-only rule: the held-read design was tried on the check host and froze every other read of the view, so the clock stays for serial hosts.
New test-side rule: silent test writes look like broken readers once handlers stop polling, and the announce call must run off the event loop.
Adds the burst-test-plus-mutation procedure that proved the filters on the MCP server, which the skill only partly describes.
Records the chassis gap left open by ticket code.server.tool#14 and the project and table filter the watcher uses.

Session added memory's own file watcher because no project-wide file-change event exists; the handler rules did not say where a source-file change comes from or how to prove the watcher idle. Patching the existing event-handler skill keeps the rule with its siblings.

The held-runner fix made stay_connected scan every system session, and the scan stayed cheap only because holding() filters each row by its own state before any read. That filter-first step is a reusable handler rule, not only a dispatch detail.
